experience.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)
experience.summary: Work directly with VA stakeholders on a healthcare claims platform with two frontends sharing a database, supporting claim submission, provider updates, claim progress and status tracking, and payment visibility.
highlights: Work directly with VA stakeholders to map healthcare claims workflows, clarify technical and operational constraints, and define requirements and acceptance criteria for claim submission, provider updates, status tracking, and payment visibility.

Lead the stakeholder demonstrations at the end of each release cycle and program increment (since 2022) and all discussions with VA stakeholders; gather feedback on daily workflows and refine implementations around user needs.
Join working sessions with health-provider claims processors and, at times, VA end users on issues reported in production, to see the full picture and keep future work pointed in the right direction.

Work with health providers to integrate APIs with the VA system so live claim statuses display for VA staff, providers, and veterans based on their role; the VA side previously had no continuously updated claim status.

Responded to stakeholder questions about stalled claims and process gaps by creating a claims framework that notifies the right party when a claim needs extra work, keeping claims moving and giving better tracking of every claim.

Enabled the team to use Tableau for requests and system information so any user can build their own dashboard; built custom dashboards for VA and internal users and, through repeated VA stakeholder discussions, expanded Tableau into the main way to monitor server health and system status.
Contribute React, TypeScript, and JavaScript features that turn stakeholder feedback into improvements to the claims application.

Investigate defects and data discrepancies across frontend, backend, and MySQL data; coordinate with developers and stakeholders to resolve delivery dependencies, and document progress, blockers, and operational impact in Jira.

Built and continue to enhance Data Generator & File Processing because production data can't be used in VA lower environments. The team used to spend hours each day preparing data and keeping a database in every environment; now anyone can generate a full development database or up to 10,000 custom records in under 5 minutes, and the whole team uses it daily.

Run the tool like a product: versioned Windows releases built through GitHub Actions, in-app release notes, a user guide, a stakeholder overview, and release updates for the team; added Excel file processing with duplicate detection as a second workflow when team needs grew.

Evaluated alternatives to legacy automation and helped select Playwright, weighing maintainability, reuse, authentication, and restricted environment access; developed a reusable smoke and regression framework that helps QA and developers reduce production bugs and deliver stakeholder requests faster.
Use GitHub Copilot in VS Code for development, debugging, refactoring, and test creation; use Gemini, GPT models, and Claude to explore implementation approaches.

Enabled the team to use Tableau and built custom VA and internal dashboards, now the main view of server health and system status.
Contribute React, TypeScript, and JavaScript features; trace data issues across frontend, backend, MySQL.
Built Data Generator & File Processing (used daily; full dev database in under 5 minutes) and a Playwright framework that helps reduce production bugs.

projects.name: VA Claims Workflows
projects.description: Work with VA stakeholders and health providers on a healthcare claims platform with two frontends sharing a database, supporting claim submission, provider updates, live claim status, and payment visibility.
projects.challenge: VA stakeholders needed claim submission, provider updates, and payment visibility to work reliably across two frontends sharing a database. The VA side had no continuously updated claim status, claims could stall without anyone knowing why, and there was no single view of system and server health.
approach: Work directly with VA stakeholders to clarify claims workflows, requirements, acceptance criteria, and operational constraints.
Join working sessions with health-provider claims processors and, at times, VA end users on issues reported in production, to see the full picture and set the direction of future work.
Work with health providers to integrate APIs with the VA system so claim statuses display live for VA staff, providers, and veterans based on their role.

In response to stakeholder questions about stuck claims and process improvements, create a claims framework that notifies the right party when a claim needs extra work, so claims keep moving and can be tracked.

Enable the team to use Tableau for requests and system information; build custom dashboards for VA and internal users and expand Tableau's role, through repeated discussions with VA stakeholders, into the main source for monitoring server health and status.
Contribute React, JavaScript, and TypeScript frontend features supporting claim submission, provider updates, and status visibility.
Use MySQL to investigate discrepancies between application behavior and stored data across frontend and backend workflows.
Develop a reusable Playwright smoke and regression framework to validate claims workflows, reduce production bugs, and speed delivery of stakeholder requests.
Lead demonstrations at the end of each release cycle and program increment since 2022, incorporate stakeholder feedback, and coordinate defect investigations with developers.
projects.outcome: User-reported: live claim status now displays in the VA system for staff, providers, and veterans by role, where it was not continuously updated before; a claims framework notifies the right party so claims keep moving and are easier to track; and Tableau dashboards give VA internal staff a full view of system and server health. The Playwright framework helps QA and developers reduce production bugs and deliver stakeholder requests faster. These are not independently measured benchmarks.
highlights: Stakeholder discovery, working sessions, and acceptance criteria
Live claim status through health-provider API integration
Claims framework that keeps claims moving
Tableau dashboards for system and server health
Demonstrations every release cycle and program increment
React, MySQL, and Playwright delivery
projects.audience: VA staff, health-provider claims processors, veterans, and the engineering teams supporting healthcare claims workflows.
systems: Two frontends support healthcare claims workflows against a shared database.
API integration with health providers feeds claim status into the VA system, shown to staff, providers, and veterans based on role.
Tableau dashboards present requests and system information, including server health and status, for VA and internal users.
React, TypeScript, and JavaScript supply application features. MySQL investigations connect visible behavior to stored records.
Playwright provides reusable browser tests for smoke and regression validation of claims workflows.
Authentication and restricted environment access affect investigation and validation. Internal endpoints and environment details are not public.
decisions: Changes must account for shared data across two frontends; a visible UI issue can require investigation beyond the affected screen.
Stakeholder acceptance criteria guide implementation and validation within restricted environments.
Tableau became the main monitoring view because VA stakeholders repeatedly asked for one place to see system status, and self-service dashboards let users build views without waiting on developers.
The claims framework routes work to the right party instead of relying on people noticing a stalled claim.
projects.relevance: This is the core of forward deployed engineering for me: work with stakeholders and end users to find the real problem, build and integrate the fix, demo it, and make sure people can use it.

evidence.label: Documented contributions
evidence.detail: The career record documents stakeholder demonstrations, working sessions with claims processors and VA users, health-provider API integration for claim status, a claims-tracking framework, Tableau dashboards for system status, frontend contributions, MySQL investigations, and Playwright automation. Client source code, screenshots, and internal endpoints are not public.

evidence.label: Reported outcomes
evidence.detail: Live claim status by role, the claims framework, Tableau as the main monitoring view, and the demonstration cadence are user-reported, not independently measured public benchmarks.

projects.name: Data Generator & File Processing
projects.description: A JavaScript/Electron desktop application I built so developers and QA can create realistic referral data from scratch, since production data can't be used in VA lower environments, then package and upload it.
projects.challenge: Production data can't be used in VA lower environments, so developers and QA needed a repeatable way to create large volumes of realistic referral data from scratch and tailor it to their own workflows and use cases.
projects.audience: Developers and QA teams who need realistic referral data to build and test VA workflows without production records.
approach: Independently built and continue to maintain Data Generator & File Processing for generating and editing referral data.
Provide a desktop workflow for editing existing JSON, generating new files, and preparing combined data and gzip packages.
Support uploads to configured targets, with explicit status and retry handling for failed destinations.
Ship versioned Windows releases through a GitHub Actions workflow, with in-app release notes, a user guide, and a stakeholder overview.
Added Excel file processing with duplicate detection as a second workflow when the team's needs grew.
Demonstrate updates, troubleshoot daily use, and document workflows so teammates can use and extend the tool.
projects.outcome: User-reported: the whole team uses Data Generator & File Processing daily. Work that took hours each day, plus keeping a database in every environment, now takes under 5 minutes for a full development database or up to 10,000 custom records, and developers rely on the same generated data in place of production records.
highlights: Realistic data where production data can't be used
Referral data generation and editing
Versioned releases, user guide, and stakeholder overview
Second workflow added as team needs grew
systems: Electron provides the desktop window, dialogs, and IPC between the renderer and backend logic.
The file workflow reads and writes referral JSON and produces combined data and gzip archives.
Uploads use configured targets through SFTP or WinSCP. This is a desktop file-processing workflow; the VA claims application is a separate project.
The repository documents a Windows installer and a GitHub Actions release workflow. No internal targets or upload settings are published here.
decisions: A desktop application supports local file selection, processing, and packaging; it also requires Windows installation and update handling.
A sequential upload queue attempts each destination once per run, continues after a failure, and offers explicit retries for failed destinations.
Completion reporting distinguishes completed destinations from transfer-byte progress; SFTP completion checks the remote file size.
projects.relevance: This is how I handle a recurring team need: build a tool for it, connect it to the data and systems it touches, and keep supporting it as people use it.

evidence.label: Repository-documented implementation
evidence.detail: The private repository README documents Electron UI/backend separation, JSON editing and generation, gzip packaging, and upload handling. Source access requires repository permission; no public demo is available.

evidence.label: Reported team use
evidence.detail: Daily team adoption, the under-5-minute generation time, and the previous hours of daily preparation are user-reported outcomes, not independently measured public benchmarks.

projects.name: Portfolio & Career Content System
projects.description: A React and Vite site where one validated career record drives this website, the browser resume, and the generated PDF and Word resumes.
projects.challenge: I needed my career facts to match across the website, a one-page resume, and a detailed resume without copying the same text into each one.
approach: Designed a schema-validated career record consumed by every presentation channel.
Rebuilt the portfolio on the official Untitled UI React and Vite stack, preserving static pages, content validation, and resume downloads.
Generated separate PDF and DOCX formats from the same factual source while preserving channel-appropriate layout.
Added strict diagnostics, static production builds, subpath packaging checks, and explicit deployment configuration.
projects.outcome: One publishing workflow keeps the site and every resume format in sync.
highlights: Designed one structured content architecture for every career presentation channel.
Redesigned the website with free Untitled UI React components while preserving static content and accessible navigation.
Added strict diagnostics, static production builds, subpath packaging checks, and explicit deployment configuration.
Prepared separate PDF and DOCX presentation contracts without duplicating career facts.
projects.audience: Recruiters and engineers looking at my work, and me, maintaining the resume formats.
systems: One career.json record supplies React pages, project routes, and resume content. A dependency-free schema check validates required fields before publishing.
React and free Untitled UI components render through Vite at build time. Browser hydration adds interactivity; core content and links are in the generated HTML.
Python produces PDF and Word resumes. Vite packages static assets for Cloudflare; a separate build verifies the /portfolio/ GitHub Pages base path. There is no runtime API or database.
decisions: Static rendering keeps content available before JavaScript runs and avoids a service/database to operate. Career changes require a rebuild.
One factual record reduces content drift. Web and print use separate layouts because native documents cannot run React components.
Cloudflare and GitHub Pages need different asset bases. Both builds are checked; configuration alone does not prove a production deployment.
projects.relevance: A public example of how I handle data contracts, UI, document generation, and deployment. My API and integration work is described in the work projects.
